title: France: component-order robustness for FR_REGIONS, and the bis/ter house-number suffixes
headline: Reordering French address components provably cannot break state resolution: normalize_address applies the FR_REGIONS test to every component with no positional logic, so state is permutation-invariant. The only order-dependent consumer is city_last (features.py:90), and it fires only when the region component is NOT an FR_REGIONS key, so the order risk and the dictionary gap are one defect. Separately, the premise that s2/s3 use unmapped departments is largely FALSE: the four departments that carry s2/s3 geography are all already mapped, and the whole unmapped lexicon is worth at most 2.46% of the residual. And bis is a confirmed dictionary defect (69757 tokens) but small; saint is the same defect 2.4x larger.

most_important_number.meaning: France test rows whose address contains all tokens of at least one FR_REGIONS key, union-bounded over the 14 keys, across test_s1+s2+s3. Ceiling on state resolution; floor on the unresolvable share is 487453 rows (28.7677%).

component_order.verdict: state/toks/nums/pin are PROVABLY permutation-invariant; no reordering fix is needed, and none can be justified
component_order.state_test: normalize.py:333-335  if ck in smap: state = smap[ck]; continue  -- applied to every component; the loop index is never referenced
component_order.hyphen_handling: normalize.py:331 replaces [^a-z0-9& ] with a space, so 'nouvelle-aquitaine' -> 'nouvelle aquitaine' which IS an FR_REGIONS key; hyphenation is not a failure mode

work_order_examples_traced.note: byte-identical to the previous row: permutation-invariant

order_dependent_code_path.gate: normalize.py:335 continue -- a MATCHED region component never enters city_comps (normalize.py:351-352), so it can never become city_last
order_dependent_code_path.failure_mode: an UNMAPPED region component stays in city_comps in its original position; if it trails the city ('Bordeaux, Bretagne') city_last returns the region, if it leads ('Bretagne, Bordeaux') it returns the city
order_dependent_code_path.conclusion: the order risk and the FR_REGIONS dictionary gap are ONE defect; no separate reordering fix exists

fr_regions_coverage_criterion_C.criterion: U = SUM over the 14 FR_REGIONS keys of min(count of each constituent token) in addr_tokens[France]; U/rows is an UPPER bound on state resolution
fr_regions_coverage_criterion_C.reason_for_union_bound: profile discards component structure, so per-key co-occurrence within one component cannot be tested; min() per token then SUM across keys
fr_regions_coverage_criterion_C.s1_double_counting_cause: pays de la loire / loire atlantique share 'loire'; hauts de france / ile de france share 'france'

contradiction_status.my_verdict: criterion C independently reproduces the ~71.2% family within 0.14pp; a 97.44% CEILING is arithmetically incompatible with an upper bound of 71.23% on the same data, so the contradiction is criterion-driven not data-driven
contradiction_status.status: narrowed, not closed -- I did not read D077's criterion

already_checked_root_cause_challenge.claim_challenged: test_s2/test_s3 encode geography with DEPARTMENT names, and most of those departments are absent from FR_REGIONS (examples given: gironde, nord, atlantique)
already_checked_root_cause_challenge.why: gironde, nord, loire atlantique and pas de calais are ALL already FR_REGIONS keys (normalize.py:244, 244, 247, 245); the three cited examples are precisely the mapped ones

legacy_region_token_mass.caveat: 'grand' 1710 and 'est' 189 in s2 are not region names; treat as upper bound

already_checked_root_cause_challenge.inference: the >=487453-row residual is best explained by those rows having NO region/department component at all (structural), not by unmapped vocabulary (lexical). Ranks 1-260 of addr_tokens[France] for s2 contain only street names, house numbers, city names and person names.
already_checked_root_cause_challenge.decision_impact: a department-expansion project sized on the 28.77% residual would recover at most ~2.5% of it

bis_ter.verdict: both are tokenised as ALPHABETIC WORDS in atoks, not as numbers and not as noise; LEET is irrelevant; bis is the only one not neutralised for blocking
bis_ter.leet_relevance: ZERO -- LEET is defined at normalize.py:256 and has exactly one call site, normalize.py:280 inside _name_tokens, which prep.py:12 applies to business_name only; prep.py:13 calls normalize_address for the address
bis_ter.addr_canon_fr_mapping: normalize.py:211  "bis": "bis", "b": "bis", "ter": "ter", "t": "ter"  (both are identity maps; standalone b is PROMOTED to bis, standalone t to ter)
bis_ter.tokenisation: normalize.py:342 _non_alnum = [^a-z0-9]+ : '5 bis' -> ['5','bis'] ; '5bis' -> ['5bis'] one fused token. NUM_RE (:311,:336) still lifts 5 into nums so anums is right but atoks is not
bis_ter.keys_asymmetry: keys.py:14 ADDR_GENERIC contains 'ter' but NOT 'bis'; keys.py:39 deletes ADDR_GENERIC tokens before blocking, so ter is dropped and bis survives into alph (len 3 >= 3, keys.py:42) and into kind-2 blocking keys
effect_chain: '5 bis rue pierre dignac' -> atoks '5 bis rue pierre dignac'; bis is non-numeric and length 3 so it enters alph and generates kind-2 keys (keys.py:65-68), and enters qa/sa (features.py:97-98) and the addr IDF overlap wa (features.py:129)

'5bis rue pierre dignac' -> atoks contains '5bis', which is not ^\d+$, so keys.py:41 puts it in alph and NOT in nums; the house number is lost from the number-x-word blocking key entirely; the two spellings of one address produce disjoint blocking vocabularies
BOTH bis and ter dilute the FEATURE side identically because q_atoks/s_atoks (prep.py:16) are never filtered by ADDR_GENERIC; the bis/ter asymmetry is BLOCKING-ONLY
bis_ter.honest_sizing: 0.58% of listed French address-token mass. Small. Worth one line of code because the fix is one line with zero downside, not because it is large.

addr_canon_fr_vs_addr_generic.verdict: NEW DEFECT: 19 of 30 non-empty ADDR_CANON_FR outputs are absent from keys.ADDR_GENERIC

dead_addr_generic_entries_for_france.why: ADDR_CANON_FR at normalize.py:207 maps 'st'->'saint' and 'ste'->'sainte', so by the time keys.py:39 runs those tokens no longer exist in atoks. They work for the US (st->st) and are silently inert for France.

positive_control.note: 'r'->'rue' is what makes '5 r de la paix' and '5 rue de la paix' identical; the map earns its keep in s2/s3

addr_canon_fr_vs_addr_generic.scope_caveat: changing keys.ADDR_GENERIC affects BLOCKING only; q_atoks/s_atoks used by features.py are unfiltered, so the feature-side dilution (wa, a_jac, a_cont) is unchanged by any of these recommendations

gaps: Component order is NOT observable: build_profile.py:126-127 splits on ADDR_SPLIT ([,;]) and immediately flattens into one Counter, destroying component boundaries, count and position. No row-level order distribution can be derived; the component_order section is a code result plus token-mass bounds only.
The city_last mis-fire RATE is unquantifiable. Only the exposed population is bounded (245993 s2 / 243713 s3), not the fraction on which the region actually trails the city.
The 'two components both match FR_REGIONS, last wins' path (normalize.py:334, no break) is unquantifiable for the same reason.

Comma vs semicolon divergence is a live unsized bias: build_profile.py:31 ADDR_SPLIT = [,;] but normalize.py:322 splits on ',' only. BIAS DIRECTION: if semicolons occur, the profile over-splits relative to the pipeline, so the U ceilings in criterion C are OVER-estimates of pipeline state resolution and the residual is UNDER-stated. True unresolvable share is >= 28.7677%, not exactly 28.7677%.

listed addr-token mass is a LOWER bound on true token mass: build_profile.py prunes count<=1 every 8 chunks and truncates to most_common(4000). Every '% of listed mass' figure is therefore an UPPER bound on the true share.

Absence from addr_tokens[France] is not zero. Per the 4000th listed counts (23/58/60) an unlisted token has count < 23 / < 58 / < 60 and could have been pruned at count 1. The gazetteer bound uses the cut-off count, the loosest defensible reading.
No ground truth was consulted. Whether reordering actually PRESERVES MATCHING in the scored sense is not answerable without running the pipeline, which was not done.
The 71.23% / 97.44% contradiction is narrowed, not closed: I did not read D077's criterion, so I cannot state why it differs.

recommendations.action: Add 'saint' and 'sainte' to keys.ADDR_GENERIC; add or delete the dead 'st'/'ste' entries
recommendations.measured_benefit: 174895 tokens = 1.24%/1.52%/1.50% of listed French address-token mass, 2.4x the bis mass
69757 tokens = 0.58% of listed French address-token mass; also stops standalone 'b' being promoted to a 3-char content token

recommendations.action: Add the remaining uncovered ADDR_CANON_FR outputs: rte, crs, quai, res, gen, mal, bat, fbg, prof, pres, lieu, lieudit, zone, za, zi, zac
recommendations.measured_benefit: P1+P2+P3 together = 337553 tokens = 2.814% of listed French address-token mass

recommendations.action: Do NOT open a department-expansion project for FR_REGIONS sized on the 28.77% residual. Re-target at why ~35% of s2/s3 France rows appear to carry no geography component at all.
recommendations.measured_benefit: avoids mis-sizing: the entire unmapped French department lexicon is worth <= 11985 tokens <= 2.46% of the residual

recommendations.action: Reorder nothing in normalize_address. If city_last later proves to be a source of error, ADD city_first as a second feature (features.py:90) rather than changing the 'last' rule.
recommendations.measured_benefit: avoids a rewrite of provably permutation-invariant code

recommendations.action: Record criterion C alongside the 71.10%/97.44% figures. Quote 71.23% as the ceiling and 28.77% as the floor on France's unresolvable share; never a point estimate, never a single-source rate.
recommendations.measured_benefit: closes the risk of a 97.44% ceiling being used to size a fix

The 's2/s3 use unmapped departments' root cause in already_checked is largely false: the four departments that carry s2/s3 geography are all already mapped, and the unmapped lexicon is bounded at <= 2.46% of the residual
